name: section4b_disk_farkas
purpose: Sliding and spinning disk convergence for the paper's section 4.2.

source: Masterjohn, Guoy, Shepherd and Castro, Velocity Level Approximation of
Pressure Field Contact Patches, RA-L 2022 (arXiv:2110.04157), Sec. V-A.
modulus_note: The paper uses 1.0 GPa; this scene uses 10 MPa. The original study
checked the difference and found it irrelevant to the terminal ratio.
Stated here rather than left as a silent divergence.
protocol: The disk starts at rest, settles under gravity and compliant contact,
then receives an instantaneous velocity kick. Its z, roll and pitch
are never pinned: the free mount makes the normal load settle to mg
for every representation, so patch area rather than load is what

why: Coulomb friction drives the slip-to-spin ratio eps = |v| / (wz R) to
a universal terminal value regardless of initial conditions, so
accuracy needs no reference run at all. This is a stronger benchmark
than settling, whose closed form covers only the endpoint.
The paper's error definition, used unchanged. The reference is per
representation and never fine tetrahedra: the three converge to
different terminal ratios, 0.6319, 0.6704 and 0.6497, which sit
0.038 apart. A common tetrahedral reference would fold that constant
offset into every affine and marching-cubes error point, so the
series would flatten at the offset instead of showing an order.
Convergence order is therefore measured against a run's own family;
correctness is measured against the analytic value above.
consequence: The finest rung of each series is its own reference and has no error
point, so each series stops one point short on the error plots. The
eps* plots need no reference and carry every rung.

grid.what: Grid size at a fixed time step. Spatial convergence.
why_finest_is_0p15625: Marching cubes needs it: its patch rim is only first order, so its
area and terminal ratio are both still climbing at 0.3125 mm.
Tetrahedra and affine voxels have settled well before it and run
there only to keep every column measured against the same grid.
why_tet_extras: Tetrahedral constraint count grows like 1/h and the voxel pair like
1/h^2, so equal h is nowhere near equal cost. These rungs widen the
constraint-count axis, not the resolution axis, and are cheap: tet
stays under 500 MB even at 0.012 mm. They are kept in tables and
fits and left off the resolution charts.

dt.what: Time step at a fixed grid. Temporal convergence.
why_pinned_settle: The settle phase runs at one fixed time step for every case, so all
post-kick trajectories start from an identical settled state and the
sweep measures integration error alone rather than a different
starting condition per case. A discrete plant fixes its time step at
construction, so the runner builds a second plant and copies every
discrete state group across; the transfer is asserted rather than
inferred, because a bad handoff still yields a plausible eps curve.

eps0.what: Initial slip-to-spin ratio. Invariance of the terminal ratio.
eps0.slide_rule: |v| = eps0 * wz * R, holding the spin fixed
why_range_is_narrower_than_the_paper: The paper sweeps [0.1, 10]. A voxel SDF cannot voxelize an infinite
plane, so a long slide runs off a bounded ground box; widening the
box costs memory because the grid is sized by the box, not the disk.
At the low end the singular omega -> 0 stop does not converge under
fixed-step velocity-level integration, which the pre-SDF study found

why: Matches the integration window of the earlier study so the terminal
ratios are comparable to its numbers and to the paper's 0.653.

thickness_resolution.rule: Exclude rungs whose patch area moves away from exact
why: The isotropic voxel grid spans the disk's 1.75 mm thickness with
ceil(1.75/h) cells, so 5 mm and 2.5 mm are both one cell and
stepping between them is not refinement where the rim needs it.
Marching cubes reads 0.757, 0.636 then 0.836 of exact area across
those three rungs. Fitting an order through a reversal is
meaningless, so those rungs are dropped from fits and kept in
tables. The tolerance exists because tetrahedral area asymptotes to
1.000018 rather than exactly 1; it is not a fitting knob.
eps divides by the spin rate, so it is ill-conditioned once the disk
has nearly stopped. The terminal value is read at the last sample
still spinning above this cutoff.
Voxel grids are sized by the ground box rather than by the 12 mm disk,
so their footprint grows like h^-3. The fit reproduces the ~40 GB the
original study recorded at the finest rung, which is what validates
it. Concurrency is bounded by this rather than by cores: swapping is
what makes a machine unusable. The driver admits a case only when both
--jobs and --memory_budget_gb allow it, and runs anything at or above
--solo_gb alone.
